tracks.narration: How do you add three voltages with one op-amp? It's easier than you think.
Take the inverting op-amp and replace the single input resistor with three. Each input V k drives the same V minus node through its own R k. R f closes the feedback loop.
V minus is held at zero by the feedback. So each input contributes its own current — V k over R k — and they all converge at the same node. Their sum then flows through R f to V out.
Kirchhoff's current law at V minus gives the punchline: V out equals minus R f times the sum of V k over R k. Each input is scaled by its own ratio.
Feed in three sinewaves at different frequencies and the output traces their sum, inverted and scaled. That's an analog audio mixer in one chip.
